trends.trend: AI data centres drive the first sustained US load growth in a generation
trends.why_it_shapes_daily_life: Decides where campuses, substations and power lines appear (Northern Virginia, central Ohio, Georgia, Texas, Louisiana), which towns get construction booms, and whether new factories and homes wait in line for a grid connection.

trends.trend: Capacity scarcity and grid capex push household electricity bills up
trends.why_it_shapes_daily_life: Capacity prices at the cap in PJM and multi-billion utility capex plans flow into monthly bills; regulators' fights over who pays (data centres vs households) become kitchen-table and election issues.

trends.trend: What gets built where: gas turbines, nuclear restarts/uprates, solar+storage, transmission
trends.why_it_shapes_daily_life: Named plants with in-service dates (gas CCs for 2029-2033, restarted reactors, offshore wind, batteries) determine local jobs, air permits, land use fights and what the grid mix looks like by 2031.

trends.trend: Reliability margins thin: shortfalls against planning standards, large-load curtailment rules
trends.why_it_shapes_daily_life: Auctions clearing thousands of MW short and NERC 'high risk' areas translate into conservation alerts, emergency orders keeping old coal plants open, and rules letting grid operators switch off data centres first.

trends.trend: Fuel-price shock and normalisation: 2026 Hormuz oil crisis, cheap US gas, LNG pull
trends.why_it_shapes_daily_life: Brent above $100 in 2026 and a backwardated futures curve set petrol, diesel and heating costs; Henry Hub near $3-4 sets the marginal cost of US power and the profitability of the gas-plant build-out.

latest_edition.title: 2028/2029 Base Residual Auction Report

sources.update_cadence: Normally annual, three years forward; currently on a compressed schedule (Dec 2025, Jul 2026, Dec 2026) plus incremental auctions

accuracy.why: Suppliers take binding delivery obligations with non-performance penalties and load pays $16.4bn (T1); offers from competing suppliers clear under three-pivotal-supplier mitigation and the IMM is paid to attack the result (T2); every auction is re-marked by incremental auctions and the next BRA, with an 11-year price/reserve-margin table in the report (T3); 2028/29 supply is existing or under-construction plant (T5). latest_edition.title: Settlement prices for trade date 17 Nov 2026 (captured 18 Nov 2026)

sources.update_cadence: Continuous; daily settlement

accuracy.why: Every price is a position with margin at stake (T1), set by producers, utilities, airlines, banks and funds on both sides (T2), marked to market daily with a long published literature on forecast error - futures are roughly unbiased but only modestly better than a no-change forecast, and EIA uses them for its STEO confidence bands (T3). T4 is only partly met: contracts exist to 2031+ but the 17 Nov 2026 capture shows zero volume in most 2030-31 months, and T5 does not apply. Known caveat: backwardation embeds a risk premium during the 2026 Hormuz disruption.

richness.why: Two monthly price series (about 60 points each to Dec 2031) with seasonal shape; no narrative, places or actors beyond the delivery hubs.

ai.why: Continuously updated price: gas-for-power demand from data centres and LNG is embedded in the 2028-31 Henry Hub strip (winter months $4.2-4.7) but cannot be separated from weather, supply and the oil shock.
